RAW draft · Sources: docs/rulebook/00-STAGE1-skeleton.md (Chapter 1 scope), docs/rulebook/DS-ALIGNMENT.md

Engine: Draw Steel Heroes — use the official rules for playing the game and the Director’s role; Ghostwire remaps below.

text.markdown: One player is the **Director**. Everyone else plays a **runner** — a hero in a **crew** of professionals who take dangerous jobs for pay. The Director describes the world, plays everyone the crew meets, and runs the opposition. Players decide what their runners do.
text.content: One player is the Director. Everyone else plays a runner — a hero in a crew of professionals who take dangerous jobs for pay. The Director describes the world, plays everyone the crew meets, and runs the opposition. Players decide what their runners do.

text.markdown:
Ghostwire play moves between three modes. Each uses Draw Steel’s rules, with Ghostwire additions noted in later chapters.

| Mode | What happens | Ghostwire additions |
|---|---|---|
| **Legwork** | Getting the job, talking, investigating, sneaking, preparing | Negotiation with patrons and fixers; the Wired for information (`21`); Availability when buying gear (`08`) |
| **The run** | The operation: infiltration, combat, chases, Wired intrusion | Connection states and Trace Alert (`21`); machines and chases (`23`); chrome failures (`09`) |
| **Downtime** | Recovering, spending ¥, installing chrome and mods, training | ¥ spending and lifestyle (`08`); §Craft Projects (`10`); chrome surgery (`09`) |

text.markdown: Ghostwire uses Draw Steel’s dice. Most rolls are **Power Rolls** on two ten-sided dice (`03`).

text.markdown:
Use Draw Steel Heroes for these rules. The Ghostwire column lists anything that changes.

| Topic | Use from Draw Steel Heroes | Ghostwire |
|---|---|---|
| The Director’s role | As written | Same term: **Director** |
| Heroes | As written | Called **runners** at the table; rules still say “hero” |
| Tests, Power Rolls, edges and banes | As written | Results always written low / middle / high (`03`) |
| Combat round, turns, actions | As written | Ghostwire keywords and connection states (`04`, `21`) |
| Stamina, Recoveries, dying | As written | Cyborg System Crisis; Revenant inert state (`04`, `05`) |
| Ancestries | Replaced | **Peoples** (`05`) |
| Culture and career | Replaced | **Background** and **Profession** (`06`) |
| Kits | Pattern kept | Ghostwire Kit list; Kits need owned gear (`08`) |
| Wealth | Replaced | Tracked **¥**, Availability, and gear (`08`) |
| Treasure and magic items | Replaced | Gear, chrome, mods, and foci (`08`–`10`) |
| Perks | Pattern kept | Ghostwire perk list (`11`) |
| Classes | Replaced | Nine Ghostwire classes (`12`–`20`) |
| Projects, respite, downtime | As written | §Craft Projects; chrome surgery; lifestyle (`08`–`10`) |
| Negotiation | As written | Patrons, fixers, and level-bosses use it |
| Advancement, Victories, experience | As written | Level and echelon only; no tier ladder (`24`) |
| Malice and monsters | As written | Ghostwire Bestiary; the Wire’s Trace Alert (`25`) |

text.markdown:
- **Money is real.** Runners track ¥ and buy the gear their Kits need (`08`).
- **Chrome costs flesh.** Living runners spend Body Integrity on implants (`09`).
- **The Wired is a second battlefield.** Every runner can connect; Hackers and Technomancers live there (`21`).
- **Magic is rare and costly.** Veil casters fight chrome and Cyborgs can’t cast (`22`).
- **Machines are allies.** Anyone can run one drone; Wrenches run fleets (`23`).
text.content:
• Money is real. Runners track ¥ and buy the gear their Kits need (08).
  • Chrome costs flesh. Living runners spend Body Integrity on implants (09).
  • The Wired is a second battlefield. Every runner can connect; Hackers and Technomancers live there (21).
  • Magic is rare and costly. Veil casters fight chrome and Cyborgs can’t cast (22).
  • Machines are allies. Anyone can run one drone; Wrenches run fleets (23).
